test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Given below is a statement followed by two possible reasons numbered I and II. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the two explains the event/observation/information given in the statement.

Statement - Despite having a highly skilled workforce, Company A has not been profitable for the past three years.

I. The company is located in a region where the cost of functioning is extremely high.

II. The CEO of Company A is a well-known philanthropist.

options.text: Both I and II are possible reasons
Only II is a possible reason
Only I is a possible reason
Neither I nor II is a possible reason

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I is a possible reason**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Company A** has not been profitable despite having a highly skilled workforce.
 
• Option I states that the company is located in a region where the **cost of functioning is extremely high**.
 
• High **operational costs** can impact the profitability of a company, regardless of the skill level of the workforce.
 
• High costs can include factors such as **rent, wages, taxes, and utility expenses**.
 
• Thus, the high cost of functioning is a plausible reason for the lack of profitability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Company Location and Operational Costs**__

 __
 
• Companies in regions with high operational costs need to generate significantly higher revenues to remain profitable.
 
• Such regions may have higher costs due to **economic factors, regulatory environment**, or **geographical challenges**.
 
 
 
• **Philanthropy and Profitability**__
 
 
• Option II mentions that the CEO is a well-known philanthropist, which does not necessarily relate to company profitability.
 
• Philanthropy may involve donations and charitable activities, but this does not explain the financial performance of a company directly.
 
• While philanthropy might impact the allocation of resources, it does not inherently lead to unprofitability.
